newsitem.title: UKRAINE: New Ukraine ag minister promises to push reforms.
newsitem.headline: New Ukraine ag minister promises to push reforms.

text.p: The man who has taken on the monumental task of reforming Ukraine's Soviet-era agriculture sector promised on Thursday to push ahead with reforms until Ukraine takes its place on the world stage of grain producers.

"We will remain a grain producing nation, and that will be our chief aim, and we will be a player on the world market," Mykhailo Zubets said at his first news conference since being appointed agriculture minister earlier this week.
"We still have large problems in the development of the agricultural complex, but we are not changing the path we're following," Zubets added.

Once the breadbasket of Europe, Ukraine regularly produced annual harvests of 50 million tonnes in the Soviet era, but has seen crops steadily decline since independence in 1991 -- falls blamed on shortages of seeds, fertilisers, machinery and money.

Zubets forecast a grain harvest of 35 million tonnes this year compared to a lowly 25.4 million tonnes in 1996, and said Ukraine would export 10 million tonnes compared to exports of just over five million tonnes from last year's harvest.
Last year's low crop ruturn -- the worst in decades -- was blamed on a drought at the start of the growing season.

"We can achieve a greater grain harvest than last year," Zubets said, adding the government had allocated 1.5 billion hryvnias to purchase materials and technical resources for this year's spring sowing campaign -- triple last year's level.

In addition to his new duties, Zubets holds the post of deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, is president of the National Academy of Sciences, and leader of the Agrarian Party formed just ahead of parliamentary elections next year.
His many positions have resulted in a cool reception from Western analysts, who said the agriculture sector required one person to concentrate all energies on reforming it.
Zubets also promised to reduce a glut of sugar on the domestic market by reducing sowing of sugar beets this year.
With spring sugar beet sowing due to begin Ukraine has not yet forecast refined sugar output, but produced 3.26 million tonnes of refined sugar in the 1996-97 season.

Measures would also be taken to reduce sunflower exports, he added, since domestic margarine production was dropping. Ukraine has forecast a 2.30 million tonne sunflower seed harvest this year compared to 2.04 million tonnes last year.
Zubets said he would have time to fulfill all his tasks.
"It's not a tragedy because these are parallel positions," he said, but added: "I wish there were 26 hours in a day."
